## The job

Issue #410 (person-owned, do not close, no version bump, no release): the system posts too many comments on issue threads; consolidate where possible with **no behavioural degradation whatsoever**.

The human (yuma-seno) is the decision-maker. A `/engineer` message already on the thread said:

> **決定（yuma-seno、2026-10-29）: 調査で確定した A〜D を1つの PR で実装する。** 施策ごとにコミットを分ける。E（フッター折り）と F（minimize）は今回やらない。

Measures to implement, one commit each:

- **A.** claim merges into the ask's dispatch marker (`claim_turn.ts`) — PATCH the marker, don't POST a second comment; back-off restores the previous body instead of DELETE; a person's comment is never edited (their ask keeps a separate claim).
- **B.** merge/reject trigger comment carries `DISPATCH_TAG` and *is* the marker (`dispatch-targets.ts`) → 4 comments become 1.
- **C.** progress comment merged into the child→parent report (`app/aggregation.ts` → `sub-issue-report.ts`), edit-based; progress text must not start with `/`.
- **D.** limit notice merged into the result comment (`notify_limit_reached.ts` + runner workflow), de-duplicating the double @mention; `manage_dispatch_loop.ts` chain counting must not change.

Hard conditions from the human: A keeps the marker `include` (never brings claim's `exclude` onto it); A's restore must be idempotent (no leftover took tag); B's one-comment-two-roles must hold (restart run can read the trigger body, no double dispatch); C's read-before-edit race is harmless; D must lose no limit information when no result comment exists (failure notice is the stand-in) and the loop's chain counting must be unchanged. **If any measure risks degradation, do not implement it — report why with file:line.** Report in Japanese per measure: 何を変えたか / 何を確認したか / 残るリスク. States that mutations (minimize/edit) could not be measured live must be marked 未実測.

## Repo conventions that apply (loaded skill)

- Change `src/**` only; `dist/**` is gitignored, generated by `bun run synth`; `.github/**` comes from a release + `self/`, never hand-edited here.
- Never touch `version` in package.json.
- Checks: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (2162 tests), `bun run test:e2e`, `bun run synth`.
- Comments state *how*/*why not*; no PR/issue history in code comments; no counts that go stale.

## What is done (three commits already pushed on the branch)

1. **Claim in place (A)** — `src/entrypoints/machinery/claim_turn.ts`:
   - New exports `claimOnMarkerBody(original, {ask,run})` (appends only the took line, `src/entrypoints/machinery/claim_turn.ts:150` area) and `withoutClaimLine`.
   - `main()` reads comments via new `readComments()` (`id`, `body`, `human` via `isHumanActor`), and when the ask comment exists, is non-human and `DISPATCH_TAG.hasProse(body)`, it PATCHes (`gh api repos/.../issues/comments/{id} --method PATCH -f body=...`), then polls the read-back for the took line (existing READ_DELAYS_MS), backs off if another run's took line is present (writing nothing further), and otherwise falls through to the unchanged `raceOutcome` (which catches older separate claims on the same ask and restores the original body). Person/human or missing ask → unchanged POST path.
   - Tests in `claim_turn.test.ts`: pure body tests (include stays include, one llm-context line) plus 4 fake-gh script tests (appends and posts nothing, backs off on already-claimed marker, backs off when an overwrite happened, person's comment untouched). 18 pass.
2. **Restart directive is the marker (B)** — `src/adapters/actions/dispatch-targets.ts`:
   - Both `dispatchPostMergeAgent` and `dispatchRejectedPrAgent` now build `directive = llm-context=include \n atomaton:dispatch=<agent> \n <prose>`, post it with `commentOnWithId` (new import from `adapters/github/work-tree.ts`; `gh` import dropped), and pass `markerCommentId` to `dispatchRunner`.
   - `src/adapters/actions/dispatch.ts`: new `RunnerDispatch.markerCommentId` (documented, `:156` area), `refuseOutstandingRequest(d, markerId, ownMarker)` — the repost-when-never-visible path now runs only when `ownMarker` (i.e. when this module posted the marker); `dispatchRunner` uses `provided === "" ? postDispatchMarker(d) : provided` and `ask = d.ask ?? markerId`.
   - Tests updated: `dispatch_post_merge.test.ts` (exactly one POST to `issues/17/comments`, body contains include + dispatch tag + "merged", dispatch carries `ask=555`), `dispatch_rejected.test.ts` (directive found by body text, `atomaton:dispatch=engineer`, `ask=555`, single POST; the directive-failure test now fails the POST rule). All pass. `tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts` pins in `dispatch-targets.ts` still satisfied.
3. **Limit notice into the result comment (D)** — third commit not yet made (working tree, uncommitted):
   - `src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.ts`: new exported `makesCompletionMention(signals)` wrapping `shouldMentionOnCompletion` (used both for the comment's own mention and for the new output); new `reachedLimit()` helper; `buildCommentBody` takes `spentOn` and `buildFooter` renders it as `_<tally>_` under the cut-short line; `main()` builds `mentionSignals` + one `subIssueState` read, passes `spentOn: reachedLimit(...) ? toolCallTally(readSession(...)) : undefined`, and appends **both** `comment_id=` and `notified=<true|false>` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
   - `src/workflows/atomaton-runner.wac.ts`: `postResultCommentStep` outputs `["comment_id", "notified"]`; the "Notify that the run reached its limit" step's `if:` is now `(runtime|iterations|loop) && steps.post-result.outputs.notified != 'true'`.
   - `src/entrypoints/machinery/notify_limit_reached.ts`: header/comment text updated (now the fallback; tally lives on the report's footer). Behaviour unchanged there.
   - Tests: `post_result_comment.test.ts` gained a `describe("the run that reached a limit")` (tally in footer under the "what to do" line; absent otherwise; `makesCompletionMention` truth table) and a script-level describe (notified=true with tally when `--notify octocat`; notified=false without notify, tally still present). 72 pass in that file.
   - `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run synth` produces `if: ... && steps.post-result.outputs.notified != 'true'` in `dist/.github/workflows/atomaton-runner.yml` (dist is gitignored, do not commit).
   - A stray duplicated doc-comment ordering in `post_result_comment.ts` was fixed (doc comment stays over `cutShort`, new `reachedLimit` after it).

Earlier full-suite results: `bun run test` = 2162 pass / 0 fail; `bun run test:e2e` = 5 pass, 6 skip (many e2e need a real binary/creds). A single `tests/contract/dispatch-sites.test.ts` failure was only because `dist/` was not yet built; after `bun run synth` it passes.

## What is still open

1. **Commit 3 (measure D)** — `git add` the four files (`post_result_comment.ts`, `post_result_comment.test.ts`, `notify_limit_reached.ts`, `src/workflows/atomaton-runner.wac.ts`) and `commit_and_push` with a message explaining why (one event, one notification; the tally moved to the footer).
2. **Measure C (progress into child→parent report)** — not started. Plan formed: give `DispatchGateOptions` in `src/app/aggregation.ts:249-253` an optional recorder (e.g. `progressLine`/`onProgress`) instead of `progressMessage`, so `aggregate_sub_issues.ts` can post the report first and, when `remaining > 0`, PATCH that report comment to append the progress line (`sub-result` tag + `llm-context=exclude` line) — the gate must not post its own progress comment and must not dispatch (its `beforeDispatch`/marker path must gain the aggregate marker as today when `remaining === 0`). `reportSubIssueToParent` in `src/adapters/github/sub-issue-report.ts:103` currently returns `boolean` via `gh issue comment`; it needs to return the comment id (switching to `commentOnWithId`) and to accept an optional progress sentence, or expose a patch helper. `conclude_issue.ts:144` (`reportSubIssueToParent(repo, issue, summary)` then `dispatchOrchestratorIfSubIssueReady`) and `mcp/github.ts:826` (`reportSubIssueToParent(REPO, num, "")` then `closeIssueAndDispatch`) both need the new collaboration. The fake-gh harness cannot mutate state, so a script-level test of the two-step path is not feasible — pure-function tests of the report body plus a fake-gh test that at most one comment POST happens and a PATCH carries the progress line are what is achievable; say plainly in the PR what needed the real thing.
3. **B verification note** — the human asked for a "one comment, two roles" contract test; considered a `fetch_events` (raw-thread) test asserting the directive reaches the model and is still read as a marker by `shapedThread`/`latestAsk`, not yet written. This is a real gap to either close or name.
4. **Contract test idea not done**: `claim_turn` now reads the thread twice on a marker claim (existence + read-back/race) instead of three times. Not a correctness issue.
5. **Report requirements** — five measures in the final set (A, B, C, D = four commits) plus the honest list of what was not measured (live GitHub mutation behaviour for PATCH/edits; the double-dispatch and ordering checks only verified against fakes and pure readers). Must mention any tool error that mattered (a `edit` call failed once with "text not in file" — I re-read and used python/sed instead; no server-reported degradation). Do not claim live measurement.
6. **Ending**: after the last commit, call `create_pr(title=..., body=..., reviewer="reviewer")` — the reviewer is what actually starts the review; read `validation_dispatched` in the result and report accordingly. Do **not** close issue #410, do not bump version, do not touch `.github/**`.

## Must not forget

- Do not "fix" the markers by adding `llm-context=exclude` onto the restart directive, and do not let `claimOnMarkerBody` rewrite the llm-context line.
- Do not restore/destroy another run's claim when backing off after an overwrite (leave it in place).
- `askSuperseded` / `shapedThread` / `latestAsk` were verified to read marker + took line from one body; `wasLaunchedOn` has no caller.
- The remaining-turns instruction: if a check fails for reasons in the environment (missing dist, missing binary), rebuild or state it; do not work around silently.
- Branch work is on the PR branch created by the first commit; do not create/switch/merge branches via shell.

{"message": "Carry the limit tally on the result comment

A run that stopped at a limit produced two comments on the thread: the
result comment's "cut short, here is how to continue" and a separate
notice that mentioned the same login and said the same thing, plus
where the budget went. Two notifications for one event, on the
commonest limit path.

The tally moved onto the result comment's footer, under the
cut-short line, so nothing it said is lost. The runner then asks that
comment whether it named the person (`notified` output, derived from
the same signal that decided the comment's own mention) and runs the
notice only when it did not: the comment was skipped, nobody is
configured, or the mention was silenced by design on a closed
sub-issue. There the notice is still the stand-in, and still the one
carrier of the tally.

`manage_dispatch_loop.ts` is untouched: it counts the join comment by
its dispatch tag, which this comment does not carry, so the chain
tally reads the same before and after."}
